def test_write_rst_with_header_rows():
    """Write a table as a SimpleRST Table with multiple header rows"""
    table = QTable()
    table["wave"] = [350, 950] * u.nm
    table["response"] = [0.7, 1.2] * u.count
    out = StringIO()
    ascii.write(table, out, Writer=ascii.RST, header_rows=["name", "unit"])
    assert_equal_splitlines(
        out.getvalue(),
        """\
===== ========
 wave response
   nm       ct
===== ========
350.0      0.7
950.0      1.2
===== ========
""",
    )


def test_write_rst_with_header_rows_single():
    """Write a table as a SimpleRST Table with a single (name) header row"""
    table = QTable()
    table["wave"] = [350, 950] * u.nm
    table["response"] = [0.7, 1.2] * u.count
    out = StringIO()
    ascii.write(table, out, Writer=ascii.RST, header_rows=["name"])
    assert_equal_splitlines(
        out.getvalue(),
        """\
===== ========
 wave response
===== ========
350.0      0.7
950.0      1.2
===== ========
""",
    )

def __init__(self, header_rows=None):
        super().__init__(delimiter_pad=None, bookend=False, header_rows=header_rows)
        self.header_rows = header_rows if header_rows is not None else ["name"]

    def write(self, lines):
        # SimpleRST tables put a position line both above and below the
        # header rows, so the top border must be repeated after writing.
        lines = super().write(lines)
        position_index = len(self.header.header_rows) - 1
        lines = [lines[position_index]] + lines + [lines[position_index]]
        return lines
